page: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v7 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs built on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64). Configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, it provides an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning directly with memory-intensive compute architectures. The virtual machine includes 2835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage, while containing no hardware GPU accelerators or included public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware resource allocation delivers a balanced 1:8 core-to-memory configuration alongside dense, high-speed local disk capacity. The integrated 2835 GB NVMe SSD volume offers high-throughput, low-latency temporary storage directly attached to the host, avoiding network storage latency for scratch space, caching layers, and transient data. Because the architecture is arm64, software deployments require ARM-compatible operating systems and execution runtimes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM architecture combined with a dedicated 48-vCPU allocation delivers dense compute and memory resources designed to minimize operational overhead relative to traditional x86 allocations. The bundling of 2835 GB high-capacity local NVMe storage reduces reliance on external attached storage for temporary I/O operations, though persistent data retention requires secondary managed storage tiers.

The E48pds_v7 is suitable for memory-heavy enterprise applications, in-memory databases, large-scale distributed caching systems, and high-performance data processing pipelines. It also fits transient analytical batch jobs and staging environments that require significant RAM and rapid temporary local NVMe disk throughput.
